findings.evidence: crates/oqueue-broker/src/sync_group.rs:267-269 computes `synced` from the record `append_durably` returned and never re-reads it; crates/oqueue-broker/src/sync_group/barrier.rs `submit` guards on `a.generation > generation`, while `refuse` (barrier.rs:246-273) guards on `a.generation > generation || (a.generation == generation && a.map.is_some())`. Compare the two guards. Interleaving: `SyncComplete` -> `Stable@N`; a `LeaveGroup` fires `MemberLeft`, legal from `Stable` per group_state.rs, taking the group to `PreparingRebalance@N` and calling `refuse(g, N)` which publishes `{N, None}`; the leader's task resumes with a stale `synced == true` and `submit(g, N, map)` overwrites it. Followers then read `Known::Mine` and are answered `NONE` with a gen-N slice instead of `REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS` -- the revoke-before-reassign harm M4.42/M4.45 exist to prevent, through the writer M4.47 added.
findings.summary: The sync barrier's two writers have mirror-image guards and only one of them is symmetric: `submit` permits a same-generation write while `refuse` refuses one, so a member lost between the transition and the leader's submission has its refusal overwritten by an assignment for a generation the group has already left.

findings.evidence: crates/oqueue-broker/src/join_group/deadline.rs:21-23 clamps the client's `rebalance_timeout_ms` into `barrier_ms`, so a member asking 60_000 waits 60_000. crates/oqueue-broker/src/sync_group/deadline.rs:16 is a flat `MAX_SYNC_WAIT_MS = 3_000_000` derived from no client value, and its doc at :9-15 says it is 'Chosen equal to `join_group::deadline::MAX_BARRIER_MS` -- the same order of magnitude a real client's own `rebalance.timeout.ms` already bounds the whole join-then-sync round trip to, so this alone is never the tighter limit'. The reference consumer's `rebalance.timeout.ms` default is 300_000, so the sync ceiling is ten times looser than what the join half honours; `waited_ms=3000000` is the exact stranding M4.47's commit body proved. Compare the two files.
findings.summary: Nothing bounds the sync phase by the number the join phase is bounded by, and `MAX_SYNC_WAIT_MS`'s own doc argues the opposite of what the two modules do.

findings.evidence: crates/oqueue-broker/src/fencing.rs:1-9 says it is 'the one seam every M4.7-M4.10 handler's own fencing decision routes through' and that a handler 'never constructs one of the wire codes that decision can produce by any other path'. Sites: offset_fetch.rs:107, sync_group.rs:127, :263, :288, :307, join_group/mod.rs:52, :54, :132, plus heartbeat.rs:477 matching on a variant. Only leave_group.rs:69, heartbeat.rs:458, offset_commit.rs:387, sync_group.rs:88 and join_group/mod.rs:164 call `fence`. `grep -rn 'error_codes::(UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID|ILLEGAL_GENERATION|REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS|FENCED_INSTANCE_ID|NOT_COORDINATOR|COORDINATOR_NOT_AVAILABLE|COORDINATOR_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS)' crates/oqueue-broker/src` outside fencing.rs returns nothing, which is what makes the gate green: the narrow property holds and the stated one does not.
findings.summary: The fencing seam's stated property is not the one that holds: eight handler sites decide a refusal themselves and reach `Refusal::X.error_code()` without calling `fence`, and `check-fencing-seam.sh` cannot see them because it greps for the `error_codes::` constants those sites do not name.

findings.evidence: scripts/gates/m4-complete.sh:237 is `if group_names_a_principal "$path"; then`, and scripts/lib.sh:305-307's helper is a bare `grep -qE`, so rc 2 and rc 127 both take the else branch. Compare scripts/check-fencing-seam.sh:171-184, which takes `awk`'s status explicitly and fails with 'the UNKNOWN_SERVER_ERROR scan could not read the group handlers'. tests/gates/negative.sh:4818-4820 asserts 'rc 2 is a bad pattern or an unreadable file; 127 is a missing helper' -- the property the gate does not have. Recorded as a minor by M4.50 and routed by name to M4.59, which hardened the test's reading and left the gate's: the milestone's own instance-not-class pattern, on the leg that is M12.md task 3a's promotion signal.
findings.summary: The FR-40 tripwire reads `grep`'s exit status as a boolean, so an unreadable handler file or a renamed helper reads as 'no principal check' and the leg still prints `ok ... across 14 file(s)` -- while `check-fencing-seam.sh`, walking the same list, refuses the identical input and `negative.sh` already asserts the distinction the gate lacks.
